Let all congruences be modulo \(503\). Consider the polynomial
\[
P(x)=(1+x)^{10000}.
\]
The sum \(S_r\) is the coefficient of \(x^r\) in \(P(x)\) after reducing exponents modulo \(502\), i.e. modulo \(x^{502}-1\).

Now
\[
10000=19\cdot 503+443.
\]
In characteristic \(503\),
\[
(1+x)^{503}\equiv 1+x^{503}.
\]
Also, modulo \(x^{502}-1\), we have \(x^{503}=x\cdot x^{502}\equiv x\), so
\[
1+x^{503}\equiv 1+x.
\]
Thus
\[
(1+x)^{10000}
\equiv (1+x^{503})^{19}(1+x)^{443}
\equiv (1+x)^{19}(1+x)^{443}
=(1+x)^{462}
\pmod{x^{502}-1}.
\]
Since \(462<502\), the reduced polynomial has degree \(462\). Therefore
\[
S_r\equiv \binom{462}{r}\pmod{503}\quad (0\le r\le 462),
\]
and
\[
S_r\equiv 0\pmod{503}\quad (463\le r\le 501).
\]
For \(0\le r\le 462\), since \(462<503\), the binomial coefficient \(\binom{462}{r}\) is not divisible by \(503\). Hence the only multiples of \(503\) are
\[
S_{463},S_{464},\dots,S_{501}.
\]
The number of such integers is
\[
501-463+1=39.
\]
\[
\boxed{39}
\]
